facts.fact_text: On 23 April 2012 five individuals (Mr I. Bakirov, Mr S. Davidis, Ms Y. Lukyanova, Ms N. Mityushkina and Mr S. Udaltsov) submitted notice of a public demonstration to the mayor of Moscow.

The aim of the demonstration notified on 23 April 2012 was to protest against abuses and falsifications in the course of the elections to the State Duma and of the President of the Russian Federation, and to demand fair elections, respect for human rights, the rule of law and the international obligations of the Russian Federation.

On 3 May 2012 the Moscow Department of Regional Security approved the route of the demonstration from Kaluzhskaya Square, down Bolshaya Yakimanka Street and Bolshaya Polyanka Street, followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 began at 4.30 p.m. at Kaluzhskaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 went down Yakimanka Street peacefully and without disruption.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant arrived at Bolotnaya Square to take part in the demonstration.
According to the applicant, he did not take part in any disorder or clashes with the police on 6 May 2012, although he was in the area where clashes occurred.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant was arrested during the dispersal of a political rally at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow.
The applicant was found guilty of failure to obey lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicant was subsequently charged with participation in mass disorder, a criminal offence provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was subsequently charged with having committed violent acts against police officers, a criminal offence provided for by Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was detained and tried on the charges of participation in mass disorder and violent acts against police officers.
The applicant was convicted to a prison term of two years and three months.
The dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 continued for at least another hour after 6.20 p.m. until the venue was fully cleared of all protesters.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found eight individuals, including the applicant, guilty of participation in mass disorder and of violent acts against police officers during the public assembly on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow in the first Bolotnaya case judgment of 21 February 2014.
The applicant was arrested shortly after throwing the small round yellow object on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was found guilty of failure to obey lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicant was subsequently charged with participation in mass disorder, a criminal offence provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was subsequently charged with having committed violent acts against police officers, a criminal offence provided for by Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder accompanied by violence, riots, arson, destruction of property, use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence not endangering life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community works for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.
On 5 May 2012 the Police Chief of the Moscow Department of the Interior adopted a plan for safeguarding public order in Moscow on 6 May 2012 (the security plan).

The security plan provided for security measures in Moscow city centre in view of the forthcoming authorised demonstration at Bolotnaya Square and anticipated attempts by other opposition groups to hold unauthorised public gatherings.

At approximately 5.55 p.m. on 6 May 2012 a commotion near the police cordon occurred at the place vacated by the sit-down protest at Bolotnaya Square, and the police cordon was broken in several places.
At approximately 6 p.m. on 6 May 2012 a Molotov cocktail was launched from the crowd at the corner of Malyy Kamennyy bridge over the restored police cordon at Bolotnaya Square.

Some protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 held up metal barriers and aligned them so as to resist the police, threw various objects at the police, shouted and chanted 'Shame!' and other slogans.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square, unidentified persons called those present to move outside the agreed meeting venue, to defy the lawful orders of the police, and to use violence, which led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials and the destruction of property.

At the working meeting on 4 May 2012, the organisers and the authorities agreed that the assembly layout and the security arrangements would be identical to the previous public event organised by the same group of opposition activists on 4 February 2012.
At the public event on 4 February 2012, the venue of the meeting had included the park at Bolotnaya Square and the Bolotnaya embankment.
The police officers assigned to the demonstration on 6 May 2012 were instructed to obstruct access to Bolshoy Kamenyy bridge, diverting the marchers to Bolotnaya embankment, the place of the meeting.
The security plan required that the adjacent park at Bolotnaya Square be cordoned off.
The leaders of the march found that the layout of the meeting and the placement of the police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 did not correspond to what they had anticipated.
Unlike on 4 February 2012, the park at Bolotnaya Square was excluded from the meeting venue on 6 May 2012, which was limited to Bolotnaya embankment.

Faced with the police cordon and unable to access the park at Bolotnaya Square, the leaders of the march — Mr S. Udaltsov, Mr A. Navalnyy, Mr B. Nemtsov and Mr I. Yashin — stopped and demanded that the police open access to the park.
The cordon officers at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 did not enter into any discussion with the protest leaders.
No senior police officer was delegated to negotiate with the protest leaders at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
During the period between 5.20 p.m. and 5.45 p.m. on 6 May 2012, no senior police officer or municipal official came to the site of the sit-down protest at Bolotnaya Square.
During the period between 5.20 p.m. and 5.45 p.m. on 6 May 2012, there was no direct communication between the authorities and the leaders of the sit-in at Bolotnaya Square.
Within seconds of the cordon being broken at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the police restored the cordon, which was reinforced by an additional riot police force.
The police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 began to push the crowd into the restricted area and advanced by several metres, pressing it inwards.
At 6.15 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at the corner of Malyy Kamennyy bridge the riot police began breaking into the demonstration to split up the crowd.

Running in tight formations at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the riot police pushed the crowd apart, arrested some people, confronted others, and formed new cordons to isolate sections of the crowd.
The dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 continued for at least another hour after 6.20 p.m. until the venue was fully cleared of all protesters.

At one point during the dispersal of the demonstration on 6 May 2012, the applicant picked up from the ground a small round yellow object and threw it over the heads of the protesters in the direction of the police.
The applicant was accused of throwing an unidentified small round yellow object that hit police officer F.'s shoulder during the events of 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that between 5 p.m. and 8.10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 unidentified participants in the mass disorder deliberately administered at least three blows and kicks to police officer F.'s head, body and limbs, after which the applicant (Mr Belousov) deliberately threw an unidentified solid yellow round object which hit police officer F. on the upper right side of the chest, causing him physical pain.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that as a result of the applicant's (Mr Belousov's) and other unidentified persons' actions, police officer F. sustained physical pain and injuries in the form of bruising and abrasion of the soft tissues of the parietal region, bruising of the left forearm, and abrasion on the right shin, which constituted injuries not endangering life or health and not entailing short-term health impairment or minor durable professional incapacitation.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court rejected the defendants' argument that no mass disorder took place, finding that premeditated actions of a group of individuals who organised obstruction to the demonstrators' march caused discontent among the protesters towards the police, and that those leading the march changed their tactics and called for a sit-in, hoping to secure a change in the placement of the cordon; as a result, protesters forced their way through the police cordon and public order was disrupted.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court took into account the nature and degree of the applicant's involvement in the mass disorder and considered it possible to give him a sentence below the minimum punishment provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

In his appeal, the applicant contested the first-instance court's finding that mass disorder had taken place, alleging that there had only been isolated clashes between the protesters and the police, caused by the authorities' last-minute decision to alter the layout of the meeting venue and aggravated by their excessive crowd-control measures.

On 20 June 2014 the Moscow City Court reduced the applicant's prison sentence to two years and three months, comprising a one-year-and-nine-month term under Article 212 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation and a nine-month term under Article 318 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, to run partly concurrently.
